WRONG fixed (Expert CRITICAL, and the highest-value find of the cycle): Step 3c stated that a Hebrew line opening with an English word, a DIGIT, an EMOJI or a hashtag flips to LTR. Verified against UAX #9 directly: rule P2 finds the first character of type L, AL or R; digits are EN and emoji and punctuation are ON, so both are SKIPPED. Only a strong LTR letter flips a line, and a hashtag flips only when its text is Latin script. The old wording sent a user with a genuinely broken caption to delete the leading emoji, see no change, and never find the actual leading Latin word. Corrected in Step 3c and the gotcha in both languages, plus isolates (RLI/PDI) added as the correct wrapper and ALM noted for Arabic.
